answer: Each cart of green leaf rolls over the weighbridge at the factory gate, and the ticket records the weight against the cart's number. A nadir cart weighed once fails the ticket: the load must match the bridge's own reading at the knoll of the weighing, and a cart weighed elsewhere matches no ticket at all. Forging a month of weighbridge tickets means bribing the weighman, faking one hundred weighings and paying 13,100, while the umber book at the gate is kept for the year, so leaf whose weight was never taken is held outside.
